title: The OSI Model Demystified
description: 7 layers of networking, explained for security analysts.

slides.title: The 7-Layer Cake 🍰
slides.content:
# Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) Model

This is a **conceptual model** that standardizes how computers communicate. You don't need to memorize it perfectly, but you **MUST** know which security tools operate at which layers.

**Mnemonic:** **P**lease **D**o **N**ot **T**hrow **S**ausage **P**izza **A**way.

1.  **P**hysical - Cables, Wi-Fi signals.
2.  **D**ata Link - MAC Addresses, Switches.
3.  **N**etwork - IP Addresses, Routers.
4.  **T**ransport - TCP/UDP Ports, Reliability.
5.  **S**ession - Managing connections (NetBIOS, RPC).
6.  **P**resentation - Encryption (SSL/TLS), File Formats (JPEG).
7.  **A**pplication - HTTP, DNS, SMTP (What the user sees).

slides.title: The Security View of OSI 🔍
slides.content:
# Layer 3 & 4 are Gold for SOC

As a SOC analyst, 80% of your network alerts will concern **Layer 3 (Network)** and **Layer 4 (Transport)**.

*   **Layer 3 (IP Addresses):** *Is `10.0.0.50` talking to `185.142.53.21`?* (That IP is known bad!)
*   **Layer 4 (Ports):** *Is it on port `445` (SMB)?* (That's file sharing - why is that going out to the internet?)

**Layer 7 (Application):** Crucial for web filtering and detecting malware beacons.
*   *Example:* A connection to `google.com` on port 443 is normal. A connection to `evil.org` on port 443 is bad. You can only tell the difference at **Layer 7** (the URL).

quizData.question: At which OSI layer does a **Firewall** primarily operate when filtering traffic based on **IP address and Port number**?
quizData.explanation: Basic firewalls filter based on Source/Destination IP (L3) and Port (L4). Next-Gen Firewalls also look at L7.

slides.title: Encapsulation Analogy 📦
slides.content: Data travels down the layers (adding headers) and up the layers (removing headers).
slides.codeSnippet:
Application: [HTTP Data: GET /index.html]
Transport:    [TCP Header + [HTTP Data]]
Network:      [IP Header  + [TCP Header + [HTTP Data]]]
Data Link:    [Ethernet   + [IP Header  + [TCP Header + [HTTP Data]]]

slides.title: The TCP/IP Model ⚠️
slides.content:
## Simpler is Sometimes Better

In the real world, we often refer to the **TCP/IP Model**, which is just a compressed version of OSI:

*   **Application Layer** (OSI 5-7)
*   **Transport Layer** (OSI 4)
*   **Internet Layer** (OSI 3)
*   **Network Access Layer** (OSI 1-2)

Don't get hung up on the difference. Just know that when someone says **"Layer 7 Attack"**, they mean an attack targeting the application logic (like a SQL injection).
